books.title: The Silver Lining Of Xavier Reeds
books.description: A look into a world crumbling down and the person who must decide what survives.

chapters.title: Prologue: The Abyss Remembers
chapters.summary: Xavier confronts the silence left behind after the abyss disappears.
sample: The abyss is dead. I killed it.
I tore it apart, watched it collapse, felt it vanish into nothing. And yet, I can still hear it.
It whispers in the dark, in the empty spaces between thoughts. In the silence of forgotten places.
The abyss is dead. But something remains. And I am beginning to wonder: did I destroy it, or did I become it?

chapters.title: Chapter 1: The Illusion of Reedsworth
chapters.summary: A familiar city reveals the first signs that reality is changing.
sample: Reedsworth appeared peaceful from a distance, but Xavier knew better.
Every window reflected a different sky, and every street seemed to remember a different name.

chapters.title: Prologue
chapters.summary: Two travelers meet at a station where every departure feels like a beginning.
sample:
The universe was not birthed from an explosion, but from a whisper. Before the first sun ignited, there was the Script—a living, breathing language that dictated the placement of every atom. To speak it was to command reality; to write it was to forge destiny.
But languages, like empires, can be fractured.
The Great Severance split the word into two warring echoes. In the high reaches of the Septum Astraea, the Archangels hoarded the "Grace-Glyphs," using the language of hope to build gilded cages they called heavens. Below, in the jagged, suffocating depths of the Aetherial Severance, the Sins twisted the script into "Void-Runes," fueled by the raw, agonizing power of fear.
For eons, the cycle was absolute. Light clashed against Dark, and the Scroll of Astraea recorded every death, every betrayal, and every predictable victory. The Story was set. The ending was written.
Until the Seventh Territory produced a mistake.
In the heart of Lucifer’s domain—a place of obsidian spires and ash-choked winds—a child was born. He was not meant to be. He was a biological paradox, the result of a moment where Uriel’s forbidden grace touched the Morning Star’s cold shadow.
When the boy took his first breath, the Great Scroll in the celestial library didn’t just record the event. It bled. A drop of violet ink fell onto the parchment, blurring the lines of the prophecy.
He was the "Hybrid of the Seventh Glyph." He was a character who had walked off the edge of the page and into the margins. And in a world built by fear and hope, he was about to prove that the most dangerous thing in existence is a story that refuses to follow its own script.
